hook.en: A sequence lists the terms; a series adds them. What is 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100? Young Gauss found it in seconds.
hook.kn: ಅನುಕ್ರಮ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಕೂಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100 ಎಷ್ಟು? ಬಾಲಕ ಗೌಸ್ ಇದನ್ನು ಕ್ಷಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ.

objectives.en: Write a series in sigma notation

narration.en: A sequence lists the terms; a series adds them. What is 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100? Young Gauss found it in seconds.
narration.kn: ಅನುಕ್ರಮ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ; ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಕೂಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 100 ಎಷ್ಟು? ಬಾಲಕ ಗೌಸ್ ಇದನ್ನು ಕ್ಷಣಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿದ.

body.en: If $a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$ is a sequence, the expression $a_1 + a_2 + \dots + a_n$ is called a series. We write it compactly as $\sum_{k=1}^{n} a_k$. A series is finite or infinite according as the sequence is finite or infinite. $S_n$ denotes the sum of the first $n$ terms.
body.kn: ಅನುಕ್ರಮದ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು + ಚಿಹ್ನೆಯಿಂದ ಜೋಡಿಸಿದರೆ ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದನ್ನು ಸಿಗ್ಮಾ ಚಿಹ್ನೆಯಿಂದ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತವಾಗಿ ಬರೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ. Sₙ ಎಂದರೆ ಮೊದಲ n ಪದಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ.

narration.en: When we join the terms of a sequence with plus signs we get a series. The Greek letter sigma is a short way of writing that sum, and S n is the sum of the first n terms.
narration.kn: ಅನುಕ್ರಮದ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು + ಚಿಹ್ನೆಯಿಂದ ಜೋಡಿಸಿದರೆ ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದನ್ನು ಸಿಗ್ಮಾ ಚಿಹ್ನೆಯಿಂದ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತವಾಗಿ ಬರೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ. Sₙ ಎಂದರೆ ಮೊದಲ n ಪದಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ.

title.en: Sigma notation and the A.P. sum

narration.en: Sigma means add up. Put k equal to 1, 2, 3, 4 in 2k plus 1 and add the four terms.

say.en: Sigma means add up. Put k equal to 1, 2, 3, 4 in 2k plus 1 and add the four terms.
Gauss added 1 to 100 by writing the sum forwards and backwards. Each pair adds to 101, and there are 100 pairs, so twice S is 100 times 101.
If we know the sum of n terms, the nth term is S n minus S n minus 1.
The same pairing trick on any A.P. gives the sum formula. For 2, 5, 8 and so on, ten terms add to 155.

title.en: From Sₙ back to aₙ; the A.P. sum

body.en: If the sum of $n$ terms is known, then $a_1 = S_1$ and $a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 2$. Recall from Class 10: an A.P. with first term $a$ and common difference $d$ has $S_n = \frac{n}{2}[2a + (n-1)d]$.
body.kn: Sₙ ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದರೆ aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁. ಸಮಾಂತರ ಶ್ರೇಢಿಯ ಮೊತ್ತ Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n−1)d] ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಿ.

narration.en: If you know S n, subtract S n minus one to get the nth term. Also recall the A.P. sum formula from Class 10.
narration.kn: Sₙ ತಿಳಿದಿದ್ದರೆ aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁. ಸಮಾಂತರ ಶ್ರೇಢಿಯ ಮೊತ್ತ Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n−1)d] ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಿ.

title.en: Sum of an A.P. grows like a parabola

caption.en: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] is a quadratic in n. Change a, d and n and read the nth term and the sum.

narration.en: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d] is a quadratic in n. Change a, d and n and read the nth term and the sum. Make d negative: the sum rises and then falls. For which n is it largest?

tryThis.en: Make d negative: the sum rises and then falls. For which n is it largest?
Set a = 1 and d = 2: the sums are 1, 4, 9, 16 … — perfect squares.
Check that Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ equals aₙ for two values of n.

problem.en: For a sequence, Sₙ = n² + 2n. Find a₁ and aₙ.

steps.en: Check: n = 1 gives 3. The terms 3, 5, 7, … form an A.P. with d = 2.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. For a sequence, Sₙ = n² + 2n. Find a₁ and aₙ.
Let us solve this together. Evaluate Σ (2k + 1) for k = 1 to 4.

body.en: To add 1 + 2 + … + n, pair the first and last terms: each pair sums to n + 1 and there are n/2 pairs, so the sum is n(n + 1)/2. So 1 + 2 + … + 100 = 5050.

narration.en: Gauss pairing. To add 1 + 2 + … + n, pair the first and last terms: each pair sums to n + 1 and there are n/2 pairs, so the sum is n(n + 1)/2. So 1 + 2 + … + 100 = 5050.

mnemonic.en: First plus last, times half the count

narration.en: Recap. A series is the sum of the terms of a sequence; Σ is the short form. a₁ = S₁ and aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁. A.P. sum: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d].
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಎಂದರೆ ಅನುಕ್ರಮದ ಪದಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ; Σ ಅದರ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತ ರೂಪ. a₁ = S₁ ಮತ್ತು aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁. ಸಮಾಂತರ ಶ್ರೇಢಿಯ ಮೊತ್ತ: Sₙ = n/2 [2a + (n − 1)d].
